model.name: Two-way weighted kNN (analog engine)
model.kind: Unsupervised weighted k-nearest-neighbour on relief (Moon: 100 m, Mars: 500 m), two-way matching
model.trained_on: Copernicus GLO-30 + ESA WorldCover 2021 (+ MODIS MOD11A2 for thermal) vs LOLA LDEM_80S_20M (+ Diviner for thermal) for the Moon and MGS MOLA 463 m for Mars; 141 Earth sites; no labels
model.inputs: Moon: 5 km squares at 100 m pixels; Mars: 20 km squares at 500 m pixels (MOLA's resolution). Slope, steep share, roughness, crater-like dips; mission weights; no absolute elevation
model.limits: Sparse: 141 sites of 78,993 cells; unscored cells are 'not analysed', never 0. Candidates whose every square breaks a land-cover limit (forest, crops, water) were rejected and are not exported. ~30 cm rocks invisible at 100 m (Moon) or 500 m (Mars). Only 5-6 NASA sites per world to validate on: checks show the ranking is sensible, not proven. Pass/fail limits always come from the Atlas rules.
model.score_definition: Similarity, 0-1. Each square is compared with the target's squares: d = weighted distance after scaling every measurement by Earth's typical spread (1 unit = one interquartile range); similarity = exp(-d). Score = 0.5 x (the 75% percentile of the site's square similarities, each vs its 5 nearest target squares) + 0.5 x (average over target squares of exp(-distance to the site's closest square)). 1.0 = identical to the target on every weighted measurement. No Earth site gets close to the lunar south pole (steeper than any site), so about 0.6 is a strong match. NOT on the same scale as rule scores.
model.score_comparability: Compare scores within one test/target set only: each set has its own target, weights and Earth scaling, so 0.5 in one set is not 0.5 in another. score_percentile (0-100) = share of the other sites analysed in the same set that this site out-scores.
model.confidence_definition: Stability, not certainty: confidence = stable_runs / total_runs. A run is one small change (see small_change_definition); 'stable' = the site's rank moved by at most max(1, 5% of the sites ranked) places. 100% = stable in every run. uncertainty = 1 - confidence. Suggested label: 'Stable in 14/14 runs'.
model.small_change_definition: One change at a time: each weighted measurement's weight x1.2 and x0.8 (2 runs per measurement), pixels 2x bigger (Moon 100 m -> 200 m, Mars 500 m -> 1000 m), and the square grid shifted by half a square. total_runs = 2 x (weighted measurements) + 2 = 10 or 12 or 14 (it depends on how many measurements the mission weighs). Not the same as the website's +/-30% x 30 weight jitter.
model.low_evidence_rule: low_evidence = true when the site has fewer than 6 usable squares (Moon: 5 km, under 150 km2; Mars: 20 km, under 2400 km2; left after removing squares with missing data or over a land-cover limit): a lead to check, not a recommendation.
model.aggregation: Several sites in one cell: keep the highest score (--agg max), as the importer does.

validation.name: Held-out NASA sites (ltv.wheels / mons-mouton-plateau)

held_out.engine_sites: Cinder Lake Crater Field 76.5, SP Crater (JETT3) 80.4

validation.agreement_note: Note on agreement with NASA: weak. The typical NASA site beats 80% of the other sites; 5 sites picked at random do this well 5.7% of the time. NASA chooses field sites for more than terrain: road access, safety, permits and nearness to its teams and towns. This model measures terrain only, so remote craters with closer terrain can outrank NASA's sites. We did not tune the weights to push NASA's sites up: that would fit the model to the answer and make this check meaningless. Top-5 counts get stricter as more sites are added (with 100 sites, top 5 means top 5%); the percentile does not, so it is the fairer comparison between runs.
validation.population: the 103 Earth sites the engine ranked for this set (not the 78,993 website cells); percentile = share of the other ranked sites the held-out site beats (100 = first); rank on similarity alone, before the land-cover ordering
